properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent, and no option is preferred.

WHERE IT CAME FROM: art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29, items D14 and W3/W4.
- In the flo2 design "ideal knowledge graph", the designer asserted "about 10,000 facts per design" (from "roughly 4.5 edges per node"), correctly marked as asserted.
- The separate OWNER agent, with no design tools, read two design exports off disk and found 9–11 facts per node. The asserted figure was about 2× low, and storage and backup sizing rested on it.
- Marking it ASSERTED made the correction visible (W4).
- Nothing in reflow2 would have flagged it: the data was within reach, and only a second reader looked.

SEARCHED ACCEPTED INTENT FIRST:
- req:a-quantity-carries-how-it-was-obtained-and-an-unsourced-one-is-reported (accepted) makes every quantity say measured, computed or asserted, and names an unsourced one. It does not compare an assertion with a computation of the same thing.
- dec:idea-a-quantity-says-how-it-was-obtained-and-a-check-can-be-rerun (accepted) is Anthony's founding worry: "something that rules out that the AI agent just didn't make up a measurement".
This idea is the next step of that thought, not a reversal of it.

═══ OPTIONS ═══

(a) A COMPUTABLE COUNTERPART. An asserted quantity may name the computation it estimates (e.g. "facts per node over design X"). A detector runs it and reports a disagreement beyond a stated tolerance.
⚠️ Counter: naming a computation needs a query surface. That is dec:idea-a-served-read-evaluates-every-derived-relation-reflow2-computes, or a rule language that does not exist yet.

(b) A FIXED MENU OF DESIGN STATISTICS, served: nodes, facts, facts per node, edges by type and the derived ratio, over this design and any design the hub reaches. An asserted number about design sizes can cite one, and the check compares.
⚠️ Counter: it helps only with estimates about DESIGNS, which is reflow2's own domain. Estimates about other systems (latency, users) have no counterpart in reach.

(c) RELY ON A SECOND READER, and make the data reachable for one. The exercise's own result (W3) is that a separate owner caught it.
⚠️ Counter: the default mode has one agent and no second reader, and the owner in that exercise had to leave the design to read files, which is item I28.

(d) A FALSIFIER ON EVERY ASSERTION: "what would show this wrong", with loop_status listing assertions whose falsifier is reachable and was never run.
⚠️ Counter: a falsifier written in prose is not computable either. It tells a reader where to look without looking.

HONEST LIMIT: this addresses numbers ABOUT DATA the design can see. Most asserted numbers in a new design, such as operations per user or the p99 of a system not yet built, have no counterpart until something is measured, and this does nothing for them.
properties.name: OPEN — when an ASSERTED number estimates something reflow2 could compute from data it already holds (facts per design, edges per node, a derived ratio), should the design say so and compare the two, rather than wait for a second reader to catch a 2× error by hand?
